answers.answer: Set Factory cards by selecting players + 1 at random, place them face-down on the board, and return the rest without looking. Put one encounter token on each of 11 marked territories. Randomly choose one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
answers.evidence: Setup: Factory cards; one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories; one structure bonus tile; lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.

answers.answer: The character starts at home; two workers start one each on the two land-adjoined territories adjoining home; four mechs start over the Faction Mat abilities; six stars by the faction emblem; six cubes in green black-square boxes; structures in matching Player Mat boxes; recruits in bottom-row circles; remaining six workers on Produce red rectangles; action token beside Player Mat. Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw. Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins, and two objective cards.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 3–4: Faction Mat starting power/combat-card draw; Player Mat starting popularity, coins and objectives; pieces table.

answers.answer: Yes, after moving the token to a different section you may take neither action. Normally you cannot repeat a section used last turn; Rusviet may. Within a turn each selected top and bottom action is limited to once. You may use top-row gains to pay a bottom-row cost. Bottom first is prohibited if taking both. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full before choosing any amount of exposed green-box benefits; mat and upgrades determine exact costs/benefits.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: may take either, both, or neither; bottom first not allowed; full cost then as much or little benefit; top-row gains may pay bottom cost.

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls the territory and its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities; you keep the abilities even without control, except a Mill cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory. Spend resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: enemy worker alone controls; enemy units do not gain abilities; pay using resources from any territories currently controlled.

answers.answer: No: normal Move selects up to two different units, each moving one adjacent territory, so one unit cannot use both selections to move twice. A carried worker can subsequently move itself, or move onto a mech and be carried by its later move. All units can carry any number of resources; only mechs can carry any number of your workers, and never your character.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: up to two different units, one adjacent territory each; carried worker may subsequently move; all units carry resources, only mechs carry workers.

answers.answer: The Speed-enabled mech may enter, but entering a territory occupied only by enemy workers makes it stop and it cannot move again that turn. The enemy workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources; you lose one popularity per worker, but insufficient or zero popularity does not prevent retreat. Your workers cannot enter independently while enemy workers control the territory.
answers.evidence: Move: enemy workers only; character/mech may enter but stops; retreat and lose one popularity per worker, down to zero; your workers cannot enter independently.

answers.answer: After all units finish the Move action, resolve all combats before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. Your workers cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
answers.evidence: Move: finish moving other units, then resolve all combats before bottom-row action; attacker chooses multiple-combat order.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card before upgrades; Monument adds one popularity. If the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck; if both deck and discards are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources or one popularity before upgrades; Armory adds one power. Traded resources go on a controlled territory containing at least one worker; if all workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources.
answers.evidence: Bolster; Trade: costs, choices and bonuses; empty combat deck reshuffle; Trade resources placement and workers-at-home restriction.

answers.answer: Pay all exposed Produce costs in full before production, then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades. Each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that territory; new workers are taken from the Player Mat left to right and placed in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Workers exposed by production affect future Produce costs, not the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce: pay every exposed cost in full before production; take new workers left to right after payment; may decline; exposing new costs affects future actions.

answers.answer: Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in exposed Upgrade cost boxes, which varies by mat/upgrades; move one cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box to improve a top benefit and reduce a bottom cost (solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded). Deploy costs the number of metal tokens in exposed Deploy cost boxes, also mat/upgrades dependent; place a mech on a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake, and its ability then applies to your character and all mechs, not workers. Even after completing all upgrades/mechs/structures/recruits, you may still pay for a bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: Upgrade—oil; Deploy—metal; placement/effect; completed bottom action can still be paid for coins and recruit bonuses.

answers.answer: Build on a controlled territory containing your worker; only one structure total per territory, and lakes and home bases are forbidden (Factory is allowed). Structures cannot move or be destroyed. A Mill gives its bonus Produce territory only while you control its territory; enemy occupation removes your control, so it cannot produce while uncontrolled. A Mine remains your personal tunnel for your unit movement even when enemy-controlled.
answers.evidence: Build: controlled territory with worker, placement limits, cannot move/destroy; Mill only while controlled; Mine personal tunnel even when enemy-controlled.

answers.answer: Take a recruit from any bottom-row section of your Player Mat and put it permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus on your Faction Mat. The one-time choices are two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is set by the circle uncovered where the recruit was removed. For a corresponding action by you, your immediate left, or immediate right neighbor, resolve active player first, then left, then right, stopping if a sixth star ends the game. In a two-player game the opponent triggers it once, not twice.
answers.evidence: Enlist and Ongoing recruits: permanent placement; four one-time bonuses; source circle sets ongoing benefit; resolution order and two-player rule.

answers.answer: Each combatant simultaneously and secretly selects dial power from 0 to the smaller of 7 and current power, and may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech, even with zero dial power. If both have combat mech abilities, attacker resolves theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously, add dial and card values; both pay selected dial power from their Power Tracks and discard every played card face-up (card values do not cost track power). Attacker wins ties.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–4: simultaneous secret selection, dial limit, card limit, ability order, reveal, payments, attacker wins ties.

answers.answer: The winner controls the territory and resources. All losing characters, mechs, and workers retreat to their home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy permits eligible units/carried workers to retreat to adjacent lakes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none, with Polania Camaraderie's stated combat exception. A non-Saxony winner places a combat star if they have zero or one already, but none after two; Saxony places one after each victory while tokens remain. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 5–6: territory, retreat/resources, popularity, star award, and losing-player card reward.

answers.answer: After the entire Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter only if the character remains on the token territory; if contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token stays. Put all resources, workers, mechs, and structures gained on that encounter territory. Pay the printed encounter cost, but no normal action costs or mat benefits, including ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Encounters: after whole Move and all combats; contested loss leaves token; gains go to encounter territory; no additional normal action costs or mat benefits.

answers.answer: Every player's character takes one card on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning any combat), looking at available cards, choosing one, and returning the rest. Each player gets at most one permanent card; later visits cannot exchange it. A Factory card is a fifth action section with optional top then bottom and the usual section restriction (Rusviet exception); similar actions grant no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. Its bottom action moves one unit up to two territories during that Move action, or three for a Speed character/mech; Mine access and normal stops apply.
answers.evidence: Factory: every player's first finish at Factory, one permanent card; action rules and no matching mat/recruit bonuses; bottom Move distances.

answers.answer: Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, you may reveal a completed objective, and must meet all requirements at that moment. Place the star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally only one objective star is allowed; Saxony retains the second card and may score both.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements: reveal timing, requirements at reveal, both cards discarded, Saxony exception.

answers.answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades, four mechs, four structures, four recruits, all eight workers on board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two stars, subject to Saxony's exception), 18 popularity, or 16 power. A placed star is permanent even if power/popularity later falls, and another player's star never blocks your goal. Play ends immediately when someone places their sixth star.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end: listed goals; permanent star; other players do not block; sixth star ends play immediately.

answers.answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, collect its primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing the star. For a neighbor's power/popularity recruit star, finish the active action, then resolve active player, left neighbor, right neighbor, checking for game end at each step; if an earlier player placed the sixth star, later recruit stars/bonuses do not resolve. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that movement portion by returning initiating units to their origin territories; do not resolve another combat.
answers.evidence: Sixth star: bottom-row benefit/coins/recruit before star; ordered neighbor resolution and pending battle movement undone.

answers.answer: At popularity 10, the 7–12 tier pays $4 per star, $3 per territory count, and $2 per complete pair of resources. Thus five stars add $20; four normal territories plus the Factory count as 7, adding $21; 13 resources make six complete pairs, adding $12. Together these categories add $53 to held coins, before any structure bonus. Your structures qualify for the selected structure bonus even when enemies control their territories. Tiebreakers: workers + mechs + structures (not character), power, popularity, controlled resources, controlled territories, then stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune: 7–12 payout rates; Factory counts three; resources paired; structures score even if enemies control; tie order.

answers.answer: A home base is not a territory for any game effect. Normally you cannot move into any home base, build there, or deploy there; setup, forced retreats, and Crimea's unlocked Wayfare are exceptions. Expansion placeholder bases without matching core factions are inactive.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: home base not territory; entry/build/deploy restrictions and exceptions; inactive expansion placeholders.

answers.answer: Mountains produce metal, tundra oil, farms food, forests wood, and villages workers; lakes and the Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.
answers.evidence: Produce terrain table; control/resources: only wood, food, metal, oil are resources; no supply limit, use multipliers.

answers.answer: Units may pick up and drop resources mid-movement; mechs can also pick up/drop workers mid-movement. A mech cannot carry your character. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character/mech, not workers; a tunnel jump costs one step, and the extra step may be before or after it. Enemy-unit and character-encounter stops override Speed.
answers.evidence: Move: all units carry resources; mech may carry workers mid-movement; Speed and tunnel step; stops override Speed.

answers.answer: Yes. Any unit may enter a territory occupied only by an enemy structure, taking control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.
answers.evidence: Move: enemy structure only; printed tunnel territories adjacent for any unit.

answers.answer: You may not pay a partial Produce cost. If unable to afford any action, legally take a dead turn: move the token to a different section and take neither action.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: never pay only part of a cost; if unable to afford any action, move token to a different section and take neither.

answers.answer: A built Armory grants one power when you Trade; a built Monument grants one popularity when you Bolster. These are built-structure bonuses on matching top actions. You keep structure abilities even without control, except a Mill cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory; an enemy occupant does not gain your structure abilities.
answers.evidence: Trade/Bolster bonuses; control section says you keep structure abilities without control and enemy units do not gain them.

answers.answer: Riverwalk applies to your character and all mechs, not workers: Nordic and Saxony cross rivers to forests/mountains; Rusviet to farms/villages; Crimea to farms/tundra; Polania to villages/mountains. Nordic Swim is separate: workers alone may cross rivers to any land terrain, not lakes. Swim does not provide lake movement to Nordic mechs; Nordic mechs need unlocked Seaworthy for lakes.
answers.evidence: Faction abilities: Riverwalk destinations and units; Nordic Swim is workers alone and not lakes; Seaworthy grants lake movement.

answers.answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels, including its Mine, adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Workers cannot use these shortcuts.
answers.evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities: Underpass and Township; both specify character/mech Move actions.

answers.answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or its Mine, reducing the opponent's Power Track by two, once per combat (not per unit). Nordic Artillery may be used before combat by paying one power to reduce the opponent's power by two, likewise once per combat, not per unit.
answers.evidence: Saxony Disarm and Nordic Artillery: timing, effect, cost, and once-per-combat limits.

answers.answer: Two mechs plus three workers permit three combat cards total: the ordinary one per participating character/mech, plus one additional card total from People's Army when at least one worker is present. Workers alone never fight.
answers.evidence: Rusviet People's Army: one additional card total; two mechs and three workers allow three cards; workers alone never fight.

answers.answer: With Wayfare, Crimea's character/mechs may move from a territory or home base to its own or any inactive faction home base regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. They cannot enter an active opponent's home base.
answers.evidence: Crimea Wayfare: destinations, any distance, and active opponent base exclusion.

answers.answer: Scout steals one random opponent combat card into your hand before combat, once per combat, not per unit. Coercion lets Crimea spend one combat card as any one resource regardless of the card's value, once per turn.
answers.evidence: Crimea Wayfare/Scout and faction starting ability Coercion: random card before combat; one card as one resource once per turn.

answers.answer: Nordic Seaworthy lets character/mechs move to and from lakes and permits retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home. Polania Submerge lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and move from any lake to any other lake; it gives no Nordic-style adjacent-lake retreat exception. With either ability, a worker on a lake needs a mech to move off, and carried workers and resources cannot be left behind on the lake when the carrier leaves.
answers.evidence: Seaworthy/Submerge section: lake movement, Nordic retreat distinction, and carried pieces leaving lake.

answers.answer: Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after Polania wins combat as aggressor on its turn. It does not cover loss for driving off undefended enemy workers without combat.
answers.evidence: Polania Camaraderie: combat aggression exception; explicitly excludes undefended workers driven off without combat.

answers.answer: Meander lets Polania choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order; the first option's gain can pay the second option's cost. It is one card, with no more than two distinct options.
answers.evidence: Faction abilities: Polania Meander allows up to two different options on one encounter card, either order; first gain can pay second cost.

answers.answer: Yes, a character entering an encounter territory stops and cannot move again that turn, including during Factory Move. The encounter is resolved only after the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there.
answers.evidence: Encounters: character stops; after whole Move action and all combats; rules also apply during Factory Move.

answers.answer: Coins are not hidden, but you need not reveal their total value when asked. Combat card hand count is public; card contents are secret until revealed, and during combat you may conceal whether you committed any cards until reveal. Objective contents are secret until you reveal a completed objective.
answers.evidence: Public and hidden information table: coins, combat cards, and objectives.

answers.answer: Informal agreements are unenforceable; coins are the only tangible items exchangeable (and tournament play forbids even coin exchanges for deals/alliances). A payment cannot cancel combat after movement has initiated it by putting units onto opposing units; combat follows Move, though bribes may influence its outcome.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements: unenforceable agreements; coins only exchangeable; negotiation cannot cancel initiated combat.

answers.answer: At popularity 0–6: $3 per star, $2 per territory count, $1 per complete resource pair. At 7–12: $4, $3, $2 respectively. At 13–18: $5, $4, $3 respectively. Controlled lakes count; home bases do not. Resources score only in complete pairs, so a single leftover resource scores nothing.
answers.evidence: Final fortune popularity table; controlled lakes count, home bases do not; resource income rounds pairs down.

answers.answer: For each adjacency tile, count unique qualifying features across all your structures. Adjacent tunnels are unique printed tunnel territories, not Mines; adjacent encounters are unique printed encounter locations even if their token is gone; adjacent lakes are unique lakes. Rivers do not break adjacency. Payouts for all three: 1 feature $2; 2–3 $4; 4–5 $6; for tunnels 6 gives $9, and lakes/encounters 6–7 give $9.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus eligibility: adjacency tiles, unique features, removed encounter tokens, Mines excluded, rivers, payout bands.

answers.answer: Structures on tunnels counts structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1 pays $2, 2 pays $4, 3–4 pays $6. Structures in a row scores only your longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break it: 1 $2, 2 $4, 3 $6, 4 $9. Structures on farms/tundras counts qualifying structures combined: 1 $2, 2 $4, 3 $6, 4 $9.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus eligibility table: structures on tunnels, in a row, on farms/tundras.

answers.answer: Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.
answers.evidence: Combat step 6: attacker loses popularity per enemy worker, even workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.

answers.answer: No. A popularity star remains placed if popularity later falls, but current popularity determines final scoring. Another faction's star does not block the same achievement; each player's goal may be awarded once, with the noted combat/Saxony exceptions.
answers.evidence: Stars: permanent despite popularity drop; other players' stars never block; final scoring uses current popularity.

answers.answer: Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions clockwise in board order Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, omitting inactive factions. Relative seating matters because ongoing recruit bonuses can be triggered by the immediate left and right neighbors; active player resolves first, then left, then right.
answers.evidence: Setup: random mats and faction seating order; Ongoing recruits: immediate left/right neighbors and resolution order.

answers.answer: A river is a border between two land territories; a lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. A unit with an applicable lake-movement ability may enter the lake from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
answers.evidence: Move: river definition; lake occupies hex and ability allows entry from any surrounding land adjoining shores.

answers.answer: No. Show the encounter card to all players when drawn, show its artwork, and read its capitalized thematic text aloud. The summary says you need not read every option aloud.
answers.evidence: Encounters: show card to all, show artwork, read capitalized thematic text; need not read every option.

answers.answer: There is no limit to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: no limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.

answers.answer: The next clockwise player may begin their turn after the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, while the current player is deciding which upgrade, mech, structure, or recruit to gain.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: next clockwise player may begin after current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, during the choice.

answers.answer: No. The chosen top action and chosen bottom action are each limited to once within a turn, including for Rusviet; Rusviet's repeat permission waives only the restriction on repeating last turn's section.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: top and bottom actions each limited once within turn, including Rusviet.

answers.answer: You may gain $1 instead of moving units.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: alternatively gain $1.

answers.answer: No. Workers never return to the Player Mat; after retreat they go to their home base, and new workers are taken from the mat only as Produce allows.
answers.evidence: Produce: workers never return to Player Mat; movement rules specify retreat to home base.

answers.answer: Yes. You may attack with zero power and zero popularity, including both at zero.
answers.evidence: Combat: you may attack with zero power/popularity.

answers.answer: Yes. You may still fight after reaching the two-combat-star limit; you simply place no further combat star as a non-Saxony winner after two.
answers.evidence: Combat: may still fight after reaching combat-star limit; star award says non-Saxony with two places none.

answers.answer: A faction without Meander must choose one affordable option; it cannot decline all options. It cannot select an unaffordable coin/popularity option. It may take as little of the chosen option's benefit as desired.
answers.evidence: Encounters: must choose one affordable option; unaffordable options cannot be selected; may take as little benefit as desired.

answers.answer: No turn-order selection: both combatants choose dial power simultaneously and secretly, and card choices are also optional secret combat contributions. Reveal the dial/card totals simultaneously after selection.
answers.evidence: Combat step 1 says simultaneously and secretly choose; step 3 says reveal simultaneously.

answers.answer: Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check their recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: announce the action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.

answers.answer: No. Place a star as soon as its goal is achieved; the sixth star immediately ends play. A completed objective is an exception in timing: you may wait to reveal it, but must still meet every requirement when you reveal it on your own turn.
answers.evidence: Stars: place as soon as achieved, sixth ends immediately; Objectives: may wait to reveal, requirements met at reveal.

answers.answer: Normally no character, mech, or worker can cross rivers or enter lakes; faction and mech abilities provide exceptions.
answers.evidence: Move: units cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes; faction and mech abilities provide exceptions.

answers.answer: No. The recruit is placed permanently on an open one-time bonus space and cannot later move.
answers.evidence: Enlist: put recruit permanently on a one-time bonus; it cannot later move.

answers.answer: No. Only a character triggers an encounter; entering with a mech or worker does not resolve or remove its token.
answers.evidence: Encounters: only a character triggers an encounter.

answers.answer: A controlled Mill adds one bonus producing territory to the normal allowance: up to three territories instead of two, or up to four if the allowance is upgraded to three. Mill itself counts as one producing worker and produces according to its terrain even with no actual worker present; actual workers there each also produce normally, so Mill output is additional. It works only while you control its territory.
answers.evidence: Produce: controlled Mill adds bonus territory; Mill counts as worker; actual workers produce too; bonus allowance; control restriction.

answers.answer: You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not establish control or preserve it after your last unit leaves if you have no structure.
answers.evidence: Control: territory control requires a unit or an uncontested own structure; resources are not listed as establishing control.

answers.answer: Build costs wood; Enlist costs food.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row resources: Build—wood; Enlist—food.
